course_description:
Introduction to the principles and applications of sensory evaluation of food; instrumental assessment of food structure; the influence of food micro and macro-structure on the texture and colour of foods measured instrumentally and perceived sensorially and advanced sensory evaluation techniques.

This course is designed to provide students with an advanced understanding of food oral processing, as well as the foundational principles and applications of sensory evaluation and objective physical property measurements. These methods are essential for assessing the quality and sensory attributes of food products.

Sensory evaluation is a critical tool that uniquely captures consumer responses to product quality. This course will delve into the core principles of sensory evaluation, encompassing its methodologies, the structuring of sensory laboratories, and sophisticated data analysis techniques. Additionally, the course emphasizes the importance of measuring objective colour and texture, which are crucial for evaluating the quality of food products. Both theoretical frameworks and practical applications of these measurements will be thoroughly examined, providing a comprehensive exploration of the subject matter.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and againstﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

Additional timetable information
Each week, there will be a 2-hour lecture, a 1-hour tutorial and a two-and-a-half-hour practical.
Tutorials and Practical classes will commence from Week 2.
The practical is scheduled as a 5-hour block to allow groups to rotate through the activities. Students are not required to attend for the full session. Each group will be allocated a specific time slot, which will be communicated prior to the practical, and will spend approximately 1.5 to 2 hours in the physical assessment lab and 30 minutes in the sensory lab.

for advice.

course_aims:
To gain an in-depth understanding of the role of sensory science in food.

To understand the significance of sensory–structure relationship for successful food product development/modification, quality control and quality assurance.

learning_outcomes.description: Summarise key physiological processes in food perception.
Explain sensory evaluation methodologies, including ethical practices.
Apply sensory and physical property assessments.
Interpret data from sensory and physical property assessments.
Integrate and critique assessment results independently and in a group environment.

Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Since this is a group assessment, any extension request must be supported by 50% or more of the group members. The group must provide supporting information and, if requested, discuss the request with the course coordinator. Please review the instructions on the extension site for group tasks .

Extensions require the correct evidence/documentation to support the requested length of time of the extension.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will incur a penalty of 8 marks. This is calculated as 2 (24 hour periods) x 10% per period x 40 marks, resulting in 8 marks deducted from the student’s mark for the assessment.
Assessment deadlines are firm and must be met. Late submission without permission or non-submission of assessable work will result in penalties being applied . Late submission of assessment will only be granted for documented medical reasons, accident, bereavement, jury service and other circumstances allowed in the UQ Policies and Procedures Library (PPL).

assessment_details.task_description: PRACTICAL TASK: INDIVIDUAL ORAL REFLECTION – SENSORY EVALUATION (10%) Following submission of the Group Sensory Evaluation Report , each student will complete an individual oral reflection during their scheduled practical class. This assessment evaluates your individual understanding of the sensory evaluation project and your ability to explain, justify, and critically reflect on the work completed by your group. Students may be asked questions about any aspect of the report, including the selected sensory evaluation method, sensory evaluation session design, data analysis, methodological considerations, interpretation of findings, and the application of sensory evaluation to food product assessment. The oral reflection will be conducted individually and will normally take 8–10 minutes . Follow-up questions may be asked to clarify or further explore your responses. This assessment must be completed independently. The use of notes, generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), or Machine Translation (MT) tools during the oral assessment is not permitted . PRACTICAL TASK: INDIVIDUAL ORAL REFLECTION – PHYSICAL ASSESSMENT (10%) Following submission of the Group Physical Assessment Report , each student will complete an individual oral reflection during their scheduled practical class. Students may be asked questions about any aspect of the report, including the experimental design, colour, texture, viscosity and microstructure assessments, instrument selection and calibration, data analysis, interpretation of results, methodological limitations, and the relationship between physical properties and product quality. assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Data Analysis Overview Each week, participants will engage in a one-hour tutorial on mastering the Jamovi software and associated packages, as well as the ClustVis web tool. Students are required to bring their own laptops with Jamovi installed to the tutorial session. These tutorials are designed to provide practical, hands-on experience in analysing sensory and physical assessment data, enabling participants to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world scenarios ( Learning Outcome 3 ) and interpret the resulting data ( Learning Outcome 4 ). The structured sessions will cover various aspects of data analysis, from basic functionalities to advanced software features, ensuring a comprehensive understanding. All tutorial sessions will be recorded to accommodate different learning styles and schedules. These recordings will be made available on the course Blackboard site, allowing participants to review the material at their convenience. This ensures that everyone has the opportunity to fully grasp the content, even if they are unable to attend the live sessions. The availability of these recordings also serves as a valuable resource for revisiting complex topics and reinforcing learning throughout the course. Assessment Overview The assessment will be conducted as an In-Class Online Assessment , where participants will solve problems based on the tutorial content using the Jamovi software and ClustVis web tool. Students are required to bring their own laptops with Jamovi installed and fully charged to complete the assessment. Students are required to bring their student ID card to class for ID verification. The assessment covers key sensory and physical property data analysis techniques using Jamovi and ClustVis, including descriptive statistics, data visualisation (e.g., boxplots and bar charts), One-Way, Two-Way and Repeated Measures ANOVA, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Cluster Analysis, Heat Maps, and non-parametric tests such as Friedman. Participants will be required to apply appropriate analytical techniques to sensory and physical assessment datasets ( Learning Outcome 3 ) and interpret the resulting outputs to draw meaningful conclusions ( Learning Outcome 4 ). This assessment is worth 20% of the final course grade and assesses: Learning Outcome 3: Apply sensory and physical property assessments. Learning Outcome 4: Interpret data from sensory and physical property assessments. Criteria & Marking : Refer to the Course Blackboard Site. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Lecture Series Lecturer: SP, BD, DC, MB & NS

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 13 (03 Aug - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Practicals (Physical Assessment) In physical assessment practicals, students will use texture analyzers, colourimeters, and viscometers to measure the colour and texture of food products objectively. This hands-on experience will enhance their ability to accurately evaluate food's physical properties and improve their technical skills. Please note that there are no practical sessions scheduled for Week 1. Before the commencement of practicals in Week 2, it is essential that you complete the online Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) training and thoroughly review the Practical Assessment Manual.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 13 (03 Aug - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Practicals (Sensory Evaluation) In the sensory practicals, students will gain practical experience with the three fundamental methods of food sensory evaluation: discriminative, descriptive, and affective. Each method assesses distinct aspects of sensory perception, essential for a thorough understanding of sensory science.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 10 (03 Aug - 11 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Tutorial Series Introduction to Jamovi software. Use of the software to analyse sensory and physical measurement data.
